title: Fix the lesson, never the source
statement: When a lesson's passage and its fixed source text disagree, change the lesson, never the source.
detail: A content audit for Grade 3 reading lessons holds every visible passage to the fixed source text, rates an added, removed or replaced word as high severity, and says to update a text by replacing its file, never by editing it to match a lesson (`shadow/content-eval/SKILL.md`, `shadow/content-eval/README.md`). Aligning whole nodes reported legitimate excerpts as rewrites, so it compares each paragraph against its own window of the source.
against: A house style can require a change: the audit treats a source dash replaced by other punctuation as information, mandated by a rule against dashes in text shown to children, not a defect (`shadow/content-eval/SKILL.md`).

evidence.quote: To update a text, replace its file. Don't edit it to match a lesson: the lesson is what gets fixed.
Whole-node alignment reported both as rewrites.
| `PASSAGE-TEXT-CHANGED` | high | a word is added, removed or replaced relative to the fixed text |
Only semicolons inside exact registered quotations are exempt; unrelated authored prose remains checked. Negative regression tests cover a changed quotation and an extra semicolon.
Quotation fidelity takes precedence in this source packet
Literary quotations: exact edition verified; altered quotes and authored semicolons remain rejected.
Record one sequence-wide policy for assigned words absent from source prose. Do not mutate story text or silently substitute a validator-friendly word.
Rewriting the story, swapping the assigned word, or enlarging generic known debt are all wrong.
We have not written around this and we have not edited the story to host the word.
